top_choice_rationale: P001 honours a mature, independently reproduced invention: trapping many neutral atoms at the magic wavelength so the light shift cancels, which allows interrogation of large ensembles without Doppler or recoil broadening and brings clock stability and accuracy to the 1e-18 level. This is the step that separates it from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, provided the citation stays anchored on the lattice scheme. Katori (concept and first realisation) and Ye (taking strontium lattice clocks to the accuracy frontier) are a defensible two-name allocation, although the early-proposal priority record for Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow, Takamoto and others remains unverified. That residual risk does not outweigh a clear, well-established achievement, so an award is preferred to no award (P000).
recusal_note: No documented tie to Katori or Ye; my profile does list close ties to the atomic-physics community of the clock field, a long-running collaboration with Anne L'Huillier, the Lund attosecond group, Ursula Keller's group at ETH, and Schuch, Dahlstrom, Argenti and Indelicato, none of which involves the credited names. No recusal ground apparent for P001.
